scale.description: Candidates and voters are positioned on each axis from -2 (fully pole_a) to +2 (fully pole_b); 0 = mixed/centrist on the axis. Voter weights per axis: 0 (don't care) to 2 (care a lot). Candidate scores must carry citations and a confidence level; low-confidence scores are excluded from alignment math.

axes.title: Taxes & revenue
axes.tension: Should Washington raise more revenue from high earners and wealth to fund public services, or hold the line and cut taxes?

pole_a.label: Limit & cut taxes
pole_a.description: Oppose new taxes (income, wealth, levy-cap lifts); prioritize reducing the tax burden

pole_b.label: Tax wealth to fund services
pole_b.description: Expand progressive revenue (millionaires tax, wealth tax, cap lifts) to fund public investment

axes.salience: The single most recurrent divider: LD43 senate (wealth-tax spread), LD32, LD36 senate (repeal vs architect), LD5, every levy measure, assessor race legislative agendas

axes.title: Spending & accountability
axes.tension: Is the bigger problem that government under-invests, or that it doesn't manage and audit what it already spends?

pole_a.label: Audit & restrain
pole_a.description: Oversight, audits, performance standards, and restraint before any new spending

pole_b.label: Invest & expand
pole_b.description: Expand programs and public investment as the primary lever for outcomes

axes.salience: Differentiates WITHIN parties: KCC D8 (accountability lane vs incumbent), LD32 senate (audit homelessness spending), LD33 P2, most R challengers; measures with ratchet/flexibility concerns

axes.title: Housing affordability
axes.tension: What fixes housing costs: unleashing market supply, or public investment and tenant protections?

pole_a.label: Market supply & deregulation
pole_a.description: Streamline permitting, cut red tape, let the market build; skepticism of rent regulation

pole_b.label: Public housing & tenant protections
pole_b.description: Social housing, rent stabilization, tenant right-to-counsel, public investment

axes.salience: Seattle D5 (three distinct positions), KCC D2 (social-housing levy timing), LD43 senate (rent-stabilization stringency), LD46, LD47

axes.title: Public safety & street disorder
axes.tension: Lead with enforcement and accountability, or with prevention, treatment, and non-police response?

pole_a.label: Enforcement & accountability
pole_a.description: Police staffing, prosecuting repeat offenders, mandatory treatment, clearing encampments

pole_b.label: Prevention & services
pole_b.description: Root causes, voluntary treatment, housing-first, community/non-police responders, diversion

axes.salience: Seattle D5 (sharpest), KCC D8 (three-strikes proposal), LD5 (police chief candidate), LD47, LD30; judicial races via prosecution-vs-defense formation and bail/diversion posture

axes.title: Climate & energy
axes.tension: Press forward on climate policy even when it raises costs, or prioritize energy affordability?

pole_a.label: Energy affordability first
pole_a.description: Repeal/pare back the Climate Commitment Act and gas taxes; expand all energy sources

pole_b.label: Climate action first
pole_b.description: Defend and extend carbon pricing, clean-energy transition, climate-resilient investment

axes.salience: LD36 senate (CCA architect vs repeal), LD33 P1 (eliminate CCA plank), CD9 (Basler's affordability critique), LD45 P1

axes.title: Record vs. renewal
axes.tension: Value a proven record and institutional effectiveness, or fresh perspectives and generational change?

pole_a.label: Proven record
pole_a.description: Incumbency, seniority, bills passed, institutional relationships that deliver

pole_b.label: New voices
pole_b.description: Outsider energy, generational change, lived experience over insider tenure

axes.salience: Appears in nearly every contested race; THE axis in LD37 P1, LD11 P1, CD1, CD7, and the appointment-pipeline argument in all four Supreme Court races

axes.title: Local control vs. regional consistency
axes.tension: Should decisions (zoning, schools, services) sit with the smallest local unit, or be set regionally/statewide for consistency?

pole_a.label: Local control
pole_a.description: City/parent/district control; skepticism of state mandates and regional consolidation

pole_b.label: Regional/state standards
pole_b.description: State housing mandates, regional authorities, county-level coordination

axes.salience: LD1 P2 (GMA rollback candidates), LD33 P2 (unfunded mandates), both fire-annexation measures, Covington park district

axes.title: Money & power in politics
axes.tension: How much does independence from institutional money and structural political reform matter?

pole_a.label: Work the system
pole_a.description: Coalition-building within existing party/donor structures gets results

pole_b.label: Reform the system
pole_b.description: Refuse PAC money; term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy

axes.salience: Central for Etzkorn (CD1), Gordon, Sawant/Chaudhry (CD9), Sabio-Howell (LD43), Brown (LD37), Leritz (LD5), Jacobson (KCC D8)

axes.title: Immigration & federal enforcement
axes.tension: Constrain federal immigration enforcement and protect immigrants, or prioritize enforcement and border security?

pole_a.label: Enforcement first
pole_a.description: Secure border, support ICE cooperation, enforcement of immigration law

pole_b.label: Protect immigrants
pole_b.description: Constrain ICE (masking bans, surveillance limits), sanctuary policies, legal pathways

axes.salience: CD7 (Jayapal's signature), CD9 (abolish-ICE spread), CD8 (R field), LD32 P2 (Siddiqi), LD46 senate, LD33 P1

axes.title: Healthcare system
axes.tension: Replace private insurance with a universal public system, or strengthen and fix the current system?

pole_a.label: Strengthen current system
pole_a.description: Protect ACA/Medicaid, cap drug prices, lower premiums within existing structures

pole_b.label: Single-payer transformation
pole_b.description: Medicare for All / universal public coverage as the goal

axes.salience: CD1 (three-way split), CD7, CD9 (mechanism/urgency differences), LD5 (Warmerdam single-payer), LD1 P2

axes.title: Gender, LGBTQ+ and reproductive policy
axes.tension: Should state law protect gender identity, LGBTQ+ rights and reproductive choice broadly (in school sports, medical care and anti-discrimination law), or set traditional sex-based and pro-life limits?

pole_a.label: Traditional values
pole_a.description: Sex-based eligibility for girls' and women's sports, limits on gender-affirming care for minors, pro-life positions, narrower anti-discrimination protections

pole_b.label: Progressive social policy
pole_b.description: Trans participation in sports by gender identity, reproductive and gender-affirming care as rights, broad anti-discrimination law

axes.salience: General ballot: I-638 (sex verification for girls' school sports) maps here. Primary evidence: LD47 P2 (DEI removal vs Members of Color Caucus chair), LD45 P1, LD41 P1, LD33 P1 (three-way spread), LD12 P2, LD46 senate. Curricula and parental-rights evidence now belongs to parental-rights.

axes.title: Parents and public schools
axes.tension: Should parents have broad notification, record access and opt-out rights over what schools teach and provide, or should schools and students have discretion?

pole_a.label: Parental notification and opt-out
pole_a.description: Parents notified of and able to review curricula, materials, records and school-provided health services; broad opt-out rights

pole_b.label: School and student discretion
pole_b.description: Educators set curricula under state standards; student privacy and confidentiality in some health and counseling matters; narrower opt-outs

axes.salience: General ballot: I-1 (parental rights in schools) maps here. Applies to state legislative contests, school-district and other school-adjacent measures, and statewide initiatives; never to judicial contests. Split from social so a voter can support one of I-1 and I-638 and oppose the other.

axes.title: AI & big tech
axes.tension: Regulate AI, data centers, and tech platforms aggressively, or keep Washington innovation-friendly?

pole_a.label: Innovation-friendly
pole_a.description: Light-touch regulation; treat tech/AI growth and its energy demand as opportunity

pole_b.label: Regulate aggressively
pole_b.description: AI guardrails, data-center limits/subsidy skepticism, platform accountability, data privacy

axes.salience: The novel axis this cycle: LD46 P1 (race's flashpoint, AI-industry money contested), LD32 P1 (Noble's platform), LD32 senate, LD45 P2, CD1 (halt data centers vs nationalize AI vs opportunity)

axes.title: Foreign policy & defense
axes.tension: Reduce military spending and conditions on aid (especially to Israel), or maintain defense commitments and alliances?

pole_a.label: Maintain commitments
pole_a.description: Strong defense budget, support allies including Israel, defense-industry partnership

pole_b.label: Reduce & recondition
pole_b.description: Arms embargo/aid conditions on Israel, audit/cut the Pentagon, end forever wars

axes.salience: CD9's clearest divider (HASC ranking member vs arms-embargo challengers), CD7 (War Powers), CD1

axes.title: Judicial philosophy
axes.tension: Should judges read law strictly as written, or pragmatically interpret it to protect rights as society changes?

pole_a.label: As written
pole_a.description: Strict construction, text and original meaning, judicial restraint, depoliticize the court

pole_b.label: Pragmatic & rights-protective
pole_b.description: State constitution as rights guarantor, law meeting the community where it is, openness to reform

axes.salience: SSC Pos 3 (clearest three-way philosophy spread), Pos 1 (rights-guarantor vs as-written), Pos 5 (posture toward Blake/bail), Pos 7 (Quinn/Blake critiques); Seattle Muni Court via bail/diversion posture

interview.authored_by: Hand-authored for this ballot from data/final/2026-11-03-general/rubric.json axes; each item maps agree -> a signed axis value. Statement directions are deliberately mixed so 'agree' alternates poles across the interview (acquiescence-bias guard).
interview.notes: value semantics: agree applies `value`, disagree applies `-value`, skip applies nothing. weight from care pulse: not-much=0.5, default=1, a-lot=2. Scenarios apply every effect listed for the chosen option. General-election changes (issue #4, 2026-10-08): card-social reworded to the narrowed social axis and flipped to value 2; card-parental-rights added with value -2 so agree keeps alternating poles (healthcare -2, social +2, parental-rights -2, tech +2, defense -2).

items.text: Washington should tax high incomes and large fortunes more to fund public services.
Before asking taxpayers for anything new, government should first prove it spends what it already has well.
The county finds a budget surplus. Where should it go first?

options.label: Hiring more police officers
options.detail: Faster response times and more patrols

items.text: The fastest fix for housing costs is cutting permits and regulations so builders can build more.
Climate policies like carbon pricing are worth it, even when they raise gas and energy prices.
I'd rather have an experienced insider who knows how to get things done than a newcomer with fresh ideas.
Two housing bills reach the governor's desk, but only one gets funded. Which one?

options.label: Cut red tape for builders
options.detail: Streamlined permits, relaxed zoning — let supply catch up

options.label: Public housing & renter protections
options.detail: Social housing dollars, rent stabilization, right to counsel

items.text: Zoning and school decisions belong with each city and community — not with the state.
I trust a candidate more when they refuse PAC and corporate money.
State and local government should limit how much they cooperate with federal immigration enforcement.
Healthcare works better when we improve the system we have, rather than replacing private insurance with one public plan.
Olympia faces a budget shortfall. What should legislators reach for first?

options.label: Cut programs & find efficiencies
options.detail: Tighten belts before touching anyone's taxes

options.label: New taxes on the wealthiest
options.detail: Protect services by asking more from those with the most

items.text: State law should protect transgender people's rights, including playing on school sports teams that match their gender identity.
Parents should be able to see their child's school records and opt their child out of lessons or school services they object to.
AI companies and data centers need much stricter rules here, even if that slows the local tech economy.
The U.S. should keep supporting allies like Israel with military aid, without adding new conditions.
Judges should stick to the exact text of the law as written — even when a strict reading produces harsh results.

care_pulse.text: How much does this issue matter to you?
